messages.subject: predict in occu( ) with polynomial functions
parts:
Dear unmarked group,

 

I fit a single season occupancy model using occu(). The model has a quadratic effect of elevation. Both elevation and elevation2 variables were standardized.

 

fm3=occu(~1~elevation+elevation2, sangelae)

Call:

occu(formula = ~1 ~ elevation + elevation2, data = sangelae)

 

Occupancy:

            Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)

(Intercept)     0.72 0.473  1.52 0.12799

elevation       2.17 0.979  2.22 0.02647

elevation2     -3.31 1.082 -3.06 0.00225

 

Detection:

 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)

      1.3 0.191 6.84 8.06e-12

 

AIC: 227.7983

 

Now I want to get predictions for this model.

 

sangelae.site

newdata1 <- data.frame(sangelae.site)

newdata1

Epsi1 <- predict(fm3, type="state", newdata=newdata1)

Epsi1

y = Epsi1$Predicted

y

y.Err=1.96*Epsi1$SE

y.Up= y + y.Err

y.Dn = y - y.Err

 

with(Epsi1, {

  plot(1:60, Predicted,type="l", lty=1,lwd=2,col="black",xaxt="n", xlim=c(0.5, 60.5), ylim=c(0, 1),xlab="Elevation (m)",

       ylab=expression(paste("Probability of occurrence (", psi, ")")),

       cex.lab=1,mgp=c(2.3,1,0),

       pch=16, cex=1.5)

  axis(1, 1:60)

})

polygon(c(1:60,rev(1:60)),c(y.Up,rev(y.Dn)),col=rgb(64,64,64,25,maxColorValue=255),border=rgb(192,192,192,25,maxColorValue=255))

 

 

By mistake I used my own data set as “newdata” and I was able to obtain a nice curve with higher probability of occupancy at middle elevations. Obviously this is not a prediction. I think that, in this case, I`m seeing the data backtrasformed, right?

 

Then I tried again, with a new data set:

 

newdata7 <- data.frame(elevation=seq(-1.8920,1.4434,length.out=60),elevation2=seq(3.57,2.083,length.out=60))

newdata7

Epsi7 <- predict(fm3, type="state", newdata=newdata7,appendData=TRUE)

Epsi7

 

plot(Predicted ~ elevation2, Epsi7, type="l", ylim=c(-0.1, 1.1),

     xlab="Elevation2",

     ylab="Expected occupancy probability")

lines(lower ~elevation2, Epsi7, type="l", col=gray(0.5))

lines(upper ~elevation2, Epsi7, type="l", col=gray(0.5))

 

But, now my predictions are incredible low and I never get a quadratic curve.

I already tried to hold one covariate as constant without success.

Anyone can help me with this?

Thanks

Best

 

Marconi Campos

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: predict in occu( ) with polynomial functions
parts:
Hi Marconi, my quick recommendation is to use the "AsIs" function in your formula for including the quadratic effect:

fm3=occu(~1 ~elevation + I(elevation^2), sangelae)

This way, you have a single covariate to work with in your predictions, especially when back-transforming for a figure.

I have standardized all variables to put them on the same scale.  

I am running into a situation when I try to do the predict function.  As Marconi mentioned in his post, when I run the predict function on my previous data, with the following code:

# eubi Adult RBP

eubi_new_data <- data.frame(cond_score_std=seq(-2.390120458,1.793241958,length.out=60),cond_score_std_x2=seq(0.006956661,5.712675804,length.out=60))    
    
preddata_eubi_RBP <- predict(eubiAfm18, type = "state", newdata=eubi_new_data, appendData = TRUE)

eubi_adult <- ggplot(preddata_eubi_RBP, aes(x=cond_score_std, y=Predicted)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), 
  alpha = 0.18) + geom_line(size=1) + theme_bw() + theme(
    line = element_line(size=1),
    axis.title = element_text(colour="black", size=24),
    axis.text = element_text(colour="black", size=16),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = unit(c(4, 0, 4, 4), "mm")),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = unit(c(0, 4, 4, 4), "mm")),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

   eubi_adult + labs(x = "Stream Condition Score", y = "Predicted Abundance")

I really don't get the same nice quadratic function that I was getting before.  I have tried holding each covariate constant by the mean and have also tried the "AsIS" function recommended by Dan Linden, but can't really get the quadratic response to overlay on the standardized stream condition score.  I can only get abundance displayed on the standardized stream score (holding condition^2 constant) or only get abundance displayed on the condition^2 scale (by holding standardized condition constant).  Anyone have any recommendations to help me display the quadratic response?

I have attached figures displaying what I am getting.  Just hoping there is a method to put this all together in a function to account for both quadratic and linear functions for both abundance and detection and so I can represent these graphically.

Thanks for the help.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: predict in occu( ) with polynomial functions
parts:
Hi Bill,

How exactly are you using the "AsIs" function?  If your lambda model is:

~cond_score_std + I(cond_score_std^2)

then your prediction dataframe only needs a single variable:

eubi_new_data <- data.frame(cond_score_std=seq(-2.4,1.8,length.out=60))

This should be able to generate the relationship you expect given the data.

Dan,

Yup, that did it.  But.. I will say it took me a bit to figure out what I had done wrong.  Prior to your recommendation, I had already created a variable for the quadratic relationship (cond_score_std_x2) in which I was trying use the "AsIs" function as I(cond_score_std_x2).  

I was getting this error:

Error in unique(c("AsIs",oldClass(x))) : object 'cond_score_std_x2' not found


I had to search around a bit before it dawned on me that you were suggesting that I use the linear condition score term (cond_score_std) and actually call on R to create the quadratic term as I(cond_score_std^2).  It worked swimmingly after I made that important correction.

Now on to telling ggplot to back-transform my x-axes to actually make my plots useable. 

Thanks!

Bill
